structured.rankingRationale: Top tier is led by multi-day future events with exact Toronto institutional venues and plausible out-of-town academic or professional participants. One-day events rank lower because room-block potential is inherently limited. Discovery 2027 ranks lowest among included candidates because the Marriott venue is confirmed; it is a future-capture/overflow monitor, not open current-edition inventory.

rejectedOrFlagged.reason: Excluded because they are already in the supplied pipeline, are mega-events without explicit overflow sourcing, or fail the university/hospital scientific focus.

notesForDeepResearch: Verify attendance, out-of-town share, housing policy, PCO/DMC and hotel RFP status before outreach.
Prioritize multi-day events with unannounced lodging: MAA, FMF200, LabFaB, IMISCOE, SWAAC, CICE and Fields UQ.
For one-day events, test speaker/VIP lodging and side-meeting value rather than assuming a room block.
materialUncertainties: No candidate source publishes a confirmed room block or peak-room requirement.
Most university and hospital events publish venue but not hotel sourcing; they are not treated as open inventory.
Attendance is generally not published, so no attendance or room-night estimates are made.
Discovery 2027 is committed to a competing Marriott venue and is included only for constrained overflow/future capture monitoring.

result.text: 13 Toronto future event-driven opportunities identified for the Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown territory, with exact verified dates and venues, sourcing posture, hotel fit, organizer leads, evidence, and explicit uncertainty handling. One competing-hotel event is correctly treated as constrained future capture/overflow monitoring rather than open inventory.
